bibliography.title: Some biological parameters and cholinesterase enzyme profile of Tilapia sp. along Maragondon River, Cavite, Philippines

method: Reviewed the full article from the publisher-hosted PDF and DergiPark-hosted PDF, then checked the journal's official open-access and copyright policy. No local PDF copy or coordinate-bearing data were retained.

sampling.collectionMethod: Haphazard and random seine-net collection, as reported by the authors.
sampling.taxonomyLimit: The authors deliberately report Tilapia sp. because of possible interspecific hybridization and limited specificity of the feral fish gene pool. Do not resolve these samples to Oreochromis niloticus or another species from this paper.

reuse.license: CC BY 4.0 per the journal's official open-access and copyright policy
reuse.attribution: Limbago et al. (2024), Aquatic Research 7(3), 155-165, https://doi.org/10.3153/AR24014; licensed under CC BY 4.0.

limitations: This is a dated sampling study, not evidence of current presence, abundance, catchability, safety, diet, or fishing legality.
The source supports only the genus-level label Tilapia sp.; no species-level taxon can be assigned from this study.
The three source-named sampling stations do not delimit the full river, establish salinity throughout it, or validate a river geometry.
The article's fish-sampling study does not establish a complete Maragondon River checklist.
nextAction: Seek a rights-clear primary source with independently supported species-level identification and a compatible Maragondon River locality; keep this 2024 study as genus-level historical context only.
